page: Microsoft Azure DC64ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V, running on an x86_64 architecture AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache layout features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction set features include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. It carries no integrated GPU accelerators.

System memory totals 256.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 2577 GB of bundled local solid-state storage along with support for Azure Premium Storage configurations. This high-capacity local SSD volume affords fast read and write access for caching layers, intermediate computational steps, and ephemeral system databases without incurring additional block storage attachments.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid aggregate compute scaling. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 68574.32, which places it in the upper quartile of multi-threaded CPU output. Conversely, stress-ng single-core performance registered at 1993.17, reflecting mid-range per-thread throughput. In memory-intensive key-value workloads, Redis SET operations reached 59.52 million operations per second, fitting into the median range. The resource footprint presents an efficient profile for parallel processing that utilizes multi-threaded CPU efficiency and abundant local solid-state capacity.

The DC64ads_v5 fits multi-threaded enterprise workloads, medium-to-large database instances, distributed cache deployments, container nodes, and continuous integration pipelines that benefit from extensive local SSD scratch space paired with standard 1:4 memory density.
description: Microsoft Azure DC64ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor. Provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores, 256.0 GB of system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and 2577 GB of bundled local SSD storage. The processor incorporates cryptographic and vector acceleration extensions, including AES, VAES, and AVX, with 32 MB of L3 cache, but excludes AVX-512 extensions. In synthetic testing, the instance logged strong multi-core compute capability, reaching 68574.32 in stress-ng multi-threaded benchmarks, alongside median-tier single-core throughput of 1993.17 and 59.52 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. With substantial local solid-state capacity and symmetrical resource distribution, the instance effectively supports distributed caching layers, enterprise database servers, multi-tenant container hosts, and parallelized compilation or ETL workloads requiring dependable scratch storage.
